pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test 'AC-1' asserts existing rows are [0,0,0] and a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the ★ prefix on the starred item and none on the others.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects only those, in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all give all items in id order.

The implementation is correct (VIEWS links in src/index.js), and the test 'each view links to the other' asserts both links. But the last commit, aae21f1 'Follow-up edits', removed the 'AC-5:' tag from that test's title, so no test names AC-5 and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. By the review rules it is unmet.
test 'AC-6' checks Starred, none, empty and __proto__ each give 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred; test 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic config check now accepts the query.

findings.what: The commit aae21f1 ('Follow-up edits', a bot commit after the builder's work) renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. This removes the only test naming AC-5, so the item is no longer named by any test. The PR body says nothing about this edit.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-5:' prefix in the test title. Explain in the PR why the follow-up commit touched it.

findings.what: The PR body claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The last commit stripped the AC-5 tag from a test title, which loosens the traceability of that test. The body does not mention it.
findings.fix: Revert the rename, or disclose it in the PR body.

lenses.note: The spec has a go from 2026-10-12. Decisions are followed: the order is unchanged, and the view is a query parameter on a GET route. Nothing was added beyond the ask.
All four state-table rows have tests (Full list, Empty table, Starred view, No starred items). AC-5 is unnamed in tests after the last commit. The spec file itself was not edited after the go.
Tests assert real behaviour. I did not run them: the Cloudflare workers test environment may be unavailable here, and CI covers them. The only gap is the missing AC-5 name.
The README describes ?show=starred. No other docs are affected.
The view selection uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ cannot select a view. The SQL is built from static strings. The traffic route regex now allows '?', which was intended.
The show value is checked against an allowlist and never interpolated into SQL or HTML. Titles are escaped. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework, styles or components; the diff touches no UI files beyond the list markup.
There is no browser flow to exercise in this review; the page is plain HTML covered by fetch-level tests.
The title is under 72 characters and the behaviour claims match the diff. The 'tests loosened: none' and 'changed after the go: nothing' claims omit the AC-5 test rename.
